# Only one publish workflow

## Pull Request by @mateuszsikora

Trusted publishing can be configured only for one workflow. We had separate workflows to publish packages on release and on push to main. This PR merges it into one `publish.yml`

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Chores**
  * Consolidated and simplified the publish pipeline for multiple packages.
  * Broadened triggers to support manual runs, pushes, and releases.
  * Added a Docker publishing step for releases.
  * Dynamically selects npm tags (latest vs next) and derives versions from package manifests.
  * Skips republishing when a version already exists; applies tags to existing versions instead.
  * Centralized release-note updates to run after publishing and removed the older redundant workflow.

<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Walkthrough

The PR removes the standalone `.github/workflows/publish-npm.yml` and expands `publish.yml` to consolidate publishing workflows: it adds a matrixed `publish-npm` job that builds and conditionally publishes multiple `@typeberry` projects (lib, jam, convert) using Node 24 with dynamic npm tagging and version checks, introduces a `publish-docker` job for release events, and adds an `update-release-notes` job that runs after publishing. Triggers, job sequencing, and permissions were adjusted; package versions are read from `dist/<project>/package.json` without appending git-hash suffixes.

## Estimated code review effort

🎯 3 (Moderate) | ⏱️ ~25 minutes

**Guard against republishing the same npm version on push + release.**  
The workflow publishes on every main push (line 5–6) and again when a release is published (line 7–8). Since the version bump PR is merged to main before the release is published, both triggers publish the same version: the push event publishes with tag "next" and the release event attempts to publish with tag "latest". npm rejects the second publish as a duplicate version.

Consider using `npm dist-tag add` to tag existing versions instead of republishing, or limit npm publishes to release events only with unique prerelease versions for push builds.

<details>
<summary>🛠️ Possible guard to avoid duplicate publish</summary>

```diff
-    - name: Publish `@typeberry/`${{ matrix.project }}
-      working-directory: ./dist/${{ matrix.project }}
-      run: npm publish --access public --tag ${{ steps.npm-tag.outputs.tag }}
+    - name: Publish `@typeberry/`${{ matrix.project }}
+      working-directory: ./dist/${{ matrix.project }}
+      run: |
+        PKG="@typeberry/${{ matrix.project }}"
+        VER=$(node -p "require('./package.json').version")
+        if npm view "$PKG@$VER" version >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+          if [[ "${{ steps.npm-tag.outputs.tag }}" == "latest" ]]; then
+            npm dist-tag add "$PKG@$VER" latest
+          else
+            echo "Skipping publish; $PKG@$VER already exists"
+          fi
+        else
+          npm publish --access public --tag ${{ steps.npm-tag.outputs.tag }}
+        fi
```
</details>

The workflow now properly guards against duplicate publishing:
